data.name: Bhairav
data.gender_notes: Bhairav is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Bhairav is a form of Lord Shiva, symbolizing fearlessness, time, and destruction. He is the remover of fear and ignorance, representing the primal, destructive force of the universe. The name Bhairav carries the meaning “Lord of Time and Fear” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bhairav usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of time and fear and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embrace fearlessness and destruction, as they are necessary for growth and transformation.
data.etymology: Bhairav belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of Time and Fear.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bhairav total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: In Hindu tradition, Bhairav is believed to occupy cremation grounds and is often invoked in rituals to ward off evil and protect the deceased during the cremation process. He is also revered as the protector of Lord Shiva's consort Parvati and is associated with the destruction of evil forces and protection of dharma (law and order).
data.spiritual_significance: Bhairav represents the destructive yet transformative power of the universe and helps us confront our deepest fears and doubts. By invoking Bhairav, we engage in an inner journey towards fearlessness and gain the courage to face life's challenges with determination and resilience.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bhairav is the fierce and terrifying aspect of Shiva, embodying raw power and destruction. He is the protector of the universe, vanquishing evil and maintaining cosmic balance.

vedic_reference.note: Bhairav is a popular name in Hinduism, and is derived from the Sanskrit word भैरव (bhairava), which means 'terrifying' or 'instilling fear'. Bhairav is a form of Lord Shiva, and is invoked to instill fear in the hearts of one's enemies.

historical_references.reference: Bhairava is a form of Shiva, associated with time and destruction. He is depicted as a terrifying figure, with multiple arms and heads, and is often shown holding a skull cup and a damaru drum. Bhairava is believed to have originated in the Hindu scriptures of the Epics period, around the 4th to 6th centuries CE.
historical_references.context: Origin and early depiction as a form of Shiva

historical_references.reference: During the medieval period, particularly in the 13th and 14th centuries, Bhairava became associated with the Bhairava Tantra, a text that emphasized the importance of fear and terror in the spiritual path. Bhairava was seen as a powerful deity who could grant blessings and protection to his devotees, particularly those seeking to overcome fear and anxiety.

trends: Bhairav is a powerful Hindu deity known for his fierce form and is often invoked when seeking protection or destruction of negative energies.
Bhairav is also revered as the lord of time and the guardian of cremation grounds, symbolizing transformation and rebirth.
platforms: Art: Bhairav is a popular subject in Indian religious art, especially in sculpture and painting.
Music: Bhairav is the name of a musical raga in Hindustani classical music, known for its melancholic and introspective nature.
Spirituality: Bhairav is widely worshipped in various forms, especially in Nepal and parts of India, where temples and shrines are dedicated to him.
modern_usage.modern_context: In modern times, Bhairav is seen as a symbol of fearlessness, courage, and protection against negative energies. His image is widely used in art, music, and spiritual practices, reflecting his enduring relevance in Hindu culture.

name_in_real_life.story: Amit Bhairav from Chennai, India embodies the meaning of Bhairav - "Lord of Time and Fear". Growing up in a Hindu family, they were taught to honor the spiritual significance of their name and live according to dharma.
